title: How Much Frosting Do You Need for Cupcakes?
summaryShort: For 24 cupcakes, plan about 3 cups of frosting for a thin spread, 4 1/2 cups for a standard swirl, and 6 cups for a tall bakery swirl. Add 10 to 15 percent extra so you never run short.
metaTitle: How Much Frosting Do You Need for Cupcakes?
metaDescription: Wondering how much frosting for 24 cupcakes? Get cups and grams for thin, standard and tall swirls, plus a scaling chart. Plan your batch now.
sidebarBullets: Thin spread: 2 tbsp (about 29 g) per cupcake.
Standard swirl: 3 tbsp (about 43 g) per cupcake.
Tall bakery swirl: 1/4 cup (about 58 g) per cupcake.
24 standard swirls need about 4 1/2 cups (1,035 g).

sections.heading: How Much Frosting Per Cupcake?
paragraphs: Plan on 2 tablespoons for a thin spread, 3 tablespoons for a standard swirl, and 1/4 cup for a tall bakery swirl. In grams, that is about 29 g, 43 g and 58 g of American buttercream.
These numbers assume a medium, fluffy buttercream that weighs about 230 g per cup. Lighter whipped frostings weigh less per cup, so weigh a test cup on your scale if you want to be exact.
list: Tall bakery swirl: 1/4 cup, about 58 g.

sections.heading: How Much Frosting Per Dozen?
paragraphs: A dozen cupcakes needs about 1 1/2 cups for a thin spread, 2 1/4 cups for a standard swirl, and 3 cups for a tall swirl. That is roughly 345 g, 518 g and 690 g.
I like to think in dozens because most recipes make 12 or 24 cupcakes. If a frosting recipe says it makes 3 cups, it covers one dozen with a tall swirl, or about 16 with a standard swirl.

sections.heading: How Much Frosting for 24 Cupcakes?
paragraphs: For 24 cupcakes, make 3 cups for a thin spread, 4 1/2 cups for a standard swirl, or 6 cups for a tall bakery swirl. In grams, that is about 690 g, 1,035 g and 1,380 g.
Most basic buttercream recipes yield only about 3 cups. So a standard swirl on 24 cupcakes needs one and a half batches, and a tall swirl needs a double batch.

sections.heading: How Piping Tip Size Changes the Amount
paragraphs: Large open star and large round tips use the most frosting, and a small tip uses the least. The wide opening lets more frosting out per inch of swirl, and you tend to pipe taller.
As a rough guide, a large open star like a 1M uses 1/4 to 1/3 cup per cupcake. A 2D star tip uses about the same, while a small star or small round tip uses closer to 3 tablespoons.
list: Small star or round tip: about 3 tbsp.
No tip, spoon and swirl: 2 to 3 tbsp.

sections.heading: Scaling for 12, 24 and 48 Cupcakes
paragraphs: Scaling is simple multiplication, but only if you start from the right swirl size. Double the dozen amount for 24, and multiply by four for 48.
The table above gives the exact cups and grams. Large batches need big mixing bowls, so for 48 cupcakes I make the frosting in two rounds rather than one huge one.

sections.heading: How Much Extra Frosting to Make
paragraphs: Make 10 to 15 percent more frosting than your chart number. You lose some in the bowl, the piping bag and your practice swirls.
For 24 standard swirls, that means about 5 to 5 1/4 cups instead of 4 1/2. Leftover buttercream keeps in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, and you can rewhip it before using.
list: Add 15 percent for piped swirls in a bag.
Add 20 percent if you are practicing a new tip or tinting several colors.

howToSteps: Count your cupcakes and choose a style: thin spread, standard swirl or tall swirl.
Multiply the per-cupcake amount by the number of cupcakes, using cups or grams.
Check the table to confirm your total for 12, 24 or 48 cupcakes.
Adjust for your piping tip, using more for large open stars and less for small tips.
Add 10 to 15 percent extra to cover bag and bowl loss.
Divide the total by your recipe yield to see how many batches to make.

faq.question: How much frosting do I need for 24 cupcakes?
faq.answer: You need about 4 1/2 cups (1,035 g) for a standard swirl. Use 3 cups for a thin spread or 6 cups for a tall bakery swirl, and add 10 to 15 percent extra.

faq.question: How many cupcakes does one batch of buttercream frost?
faq.answer: A basic batch made with 1 cup butter and about 3 1/2 to 4 cups powdered sugar yields about 3 cups. That frosts about 16 cupcakes with a standard swirl or 12 with a tall swirl.

faq.question: Do I need more frosting for a 1M tip than a 2D tip?
faq.answer: Not much. Both use about 1/4 to 1/3 cup per cupcake, though a very tall 1M swirl can run higher. Small star and small round tips use less.

faq.question: Does cream cheese or whipped cream frosting use the same amount?
faq.answer: Cream cheese frosting is similar by volume. Whipped cream frosting is lighter, so measure by cups and expect a standard swirl to use about the same volume but weigh far less.

faq.question: What if I make too much frosting?
faq.answer: Store leftover buttercream in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Let it soften, then rewhip it before piping. Use cream cheese frosting within 5 days and whipped cream frosting within 1 to 3 days.
